summary: The note examines how SMEs struggle to retain and attract skilled talent after September 2023, amid a shrinking talent pool and competition from larger firms and startups. It outlines strategies including workforce development, tailored training and apprenticeships, continuous learning culture, learning technology, government incentives, partnerships, youth engagement, and diversity and inclusion, illustrated by named company examples and expert quotes.
one_line: SMEs face a post-pandemic 'Great Talent Squeeze' and can respond with training, learning culture, technology, partnerships, youth engagement, diversity and government support.
key_facts: Labor market analyst Laura Chen coined the term "Great Talent Squeeze" for the situation where workers have the upper hand in choosing employers, often leaving SMEs out in the cold.

James Robinson, founder of TechInnovate (an SME specializing in AI-driven solutions), said on October 12, 2023: "We're no longer just competing with the business across the street; we're up against global giants and startups that offer far more than we can afford to."
Emma Watkins, CEO of construction SME GreenBuild, launched the "Skills for Tomorrow" apprenticeship program on November 3, 2023, partnering with local colleges.

Imagin8, a digital marketing firm, reported a 20% increase in retention of high-caliber staff after weaving learning into everyday tasks; Director of Learning and Development Richard Liu says "Every project should be a learning project."
TerraCode, a mid-sized software development firm, has used an AI-driven learning management system since September 2023 that adapts to each employee's skills and learning pace.

Human resources consultant Michael Stevens has worked with medium-sized firms on upscaling workforce development programs since late 2023 and says training programs, company culture narratives and growth opportunities in roles are vital.

Policy analyst Dr. Sarah Kingsley suggests government reforms such as tax credits, training grants and apprenticeship subsidies may be imminent given the recent focus on SMEs in economic recovery plans.
"Collaborate2Compete," inaugurated on September 15, 2023, is a cooperative in which renewable energy SMEs share the cost and resources of training programs; Sophia Ramirez is among its creators.
"Youth Think Tank," launched on December 5, 2023, attracts young people straight out of academia to tackle real-world business challenges under experienced mentors.
Daniel Abrams, a member of Youth Think Tank, says youth talent revitalizes projects and is a beacon for others considering where to start their careers.
Felicia Johnson, head of Diversity and Inclusion at a mid-market logistics company, says "Diverse teams are the crucibles of innovation."
Development investment has a twofold appeal: existing employees feel valued and stay, reducing turnover, and a reputation for nurturing staff attracts outside talent.
Modern recruits look beyond salary to purpose, work-life balance and career development opportunities.
